topic: The Fundamental Bridge: The Relationship Between Integrals and Derivatives

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Concept of Change
lecture_lines: Derivatives define instantaneous rates of change.
Visualize the slope of a tangent line.
Imagine a cheetah's speed at one moment.
animations: Create a point on a curve #FFFFFF labeled 'f(x)'.
Show a tangent line #FF0000 at the point.
Draw a small triangle #00FF00 illustrating dx and dy.

sections.title: The Inverse Operation: Accumulation
lecture_lines: Integrals represent the accumulation of change.
This corresponds to area under a curve.
Summing rectangles helps calculate total distance.
animations: Display a rectangle #FFFF00 under the curve #FFFFFF.
Subdivide the area into thinner rectangles.
Show the sum of areas as the width approaches zero.

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem: Connecting the Dots
lecture_lines: Integration and differentiation are inverse processes.
Like addition and subtraction for functions.
An accumulator recovers the original function.
animations: Display the derivative function #FF0000 and the integral #00FF00.
Use a morphing animation connecting the two curves.
Animate the fundamental relationship: differentiation and integration.
Show the final equation connecting both concepts.

sections.title: Visual Synthesis & Conclusion
lecture_lines: Differentiation finds the slope of curves.
The Fundamental Theorem bridges these concepts.
animations: Overlay the derivative graph onto the integral graph.
Highlight key points of intersection or correspondence.
Summarize the duality of calculus with a final graphic.
